Featured Manager · GW9

Four-and-Four, Second on Points

rmeernst has the second-best scoring side in the league and a record that says mid-table

Eight weeks in, only the leader has scored more than he has. The table has him seventh, level on wins with four other managers, and the gap between those two facts is the whole story of his autumn. Two of his four losses came by less than a goal's worth of points. Swap either one and he is sharing the lead; swap both and he is clear of it.

The scoring is not a fluke of one hot week. He has never had the biggest score of a gameweek and never the smallest, and he has not finished outside the top nine once. Tavernier, a midfielder nobody was fighting over in August, has been his best player by a distance, and this week he beat mdropkin by a point with his first two draft picks both sitting on the bench.

The model sees what the table does not. It rates his roster the second strongest in the league, a whisker behind the leader, and gives him a better title chance than half the managers above him in the table. He has thirty weeks to make the record catch up with the points.
